speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin the assessment of your walking difficulties, urinary incontinence, and speech issues, when did you first notice these symptoms appearing?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To help narrow down the cause, have you experienced any recent headaches, vision changes, or balance issues?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have described a classic triad of symptoms along with autonomic dysfunction. Do you also experience significant cognitive decline or memory loss, and have you had any episodes of fainting or dizziness upon standing?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable. No known chronic diseases. Social history: Occasionally consumes alcohol. Non-smoker. Works as a bank clerk.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your medical and social history is unremarkable, which helps rule out some secondary causes. To better characterize the rigidity and tremor, do you find that your symptoms improve with medication, or have you noticed any visual hallucinations?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent infections, fever, weight loss, vision changes or seizures.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of fever, weight loss, or seizures makes infectious or malignant causes less likely, pointing further toward a neurodegenerative process. I will now request imaging to evaluate for structural lesions or hydrocephalus that could mimic these symptoms.

REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain
REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_Puncture
